title: First Free School for the Deaf Opens in Paris
description: Abbé Charles-Michel de l'Épée founded the first free school for deaf students in Paris, developing a system of methodical signs that would influence ASL.

title: American School for the Deaf Founded
description: Thomas Hopkins Gallaudet and Laurent Clerc founded the American School for the Deaf in Hartford, Connecticut

title: Columbia Institution Founded
description: Amos Kendall and Edward Miner Gallaudet established the Columbia Institution for the Instruction of the Deaf and Dumb and the Blind (later renamed to Gallaudet University) in Washington, D.C.

title: Gallaudet University Authorized to Grant Degrees
description: President Abraham Lincoln signed a charter authorizing the Columbia Institution to grant college degrees, making it the first institution of higher education for deaf students in the world.

title: The Milan Conference and the Rise of Oralism
description: At the Second International Congress on Education of the Deaf in Milan, educators voted to ban sign language in deaf schools in favor of oral-only instruction. This decision set back deaf education and sign language use for nearly a century.

title: ASL Recognized as a True Language
description: Linguist William Stokoe published research demonstrating that American Sign Language has its own grammar and structure, distinct from English.

title: First ASL Dictionary Based on Linguistic Principles
description: Stokoe, along with Dorothy Casterline and Carl Croneberg, published 'A Dictionary of American Sign Language on Linguistic Principles,' formally documenting ASL's structure and vocabulary.

title: Deaf President Now Movement
description: Students at Gallaudet University protested the selection of a hearing president over qualified Deaf candidates. The week-long Deaf President Now movement succeeded, resulting in I. King Jordan becoming the university's first deaf president.

title: President George H.W. Bush Signs the Americans with Disabilities Act Into Law
description: The ADA prohibited discrimination based on disability and required accommodations such as sign language interpreters in many public settings, marking a major legal milestone for the Deaf community.

title: Growth of ASL in Higher Education
description: American Sign Language became increasingly recognized as meeting foreign language requirements at colleges and universities across the U.S., reflecting growing academic and cultural acceptance of ASL as a full language.

title: ASL at Notre Dame
description: Notre Dame launches an ASL class, paving the way for ASL to be accepted as a foreign language
